can_fail_a.instructions: Can a bug in the behaviour this test names make the test fail?

criteria.true: yes: some bug in that behaviour fails it
criteria.false: no: it passes whatever the code does, as with a tautology, both sides from the code, or an assertion that never runs

can_fail_c.instructions: Would some wrong output of the behaviour this test names fail it?

criteria.true: yes: a wrong output fails it

asserts_a.instructions: Of all assertions, what does the one closest to the behaviour check?

criteria.behaviour: the output, against a value the test fixes or computes without the code
criteria.from-code: the output, against a value from the code under test or a re-implementation of it in the test
criteria.input-only: only the test's own input or setup, or an output field copied straight from the input
criteria.shape-only: only type, length, keys, presence, a bound, or that it is truthy or defined
criteria.interaction-only: only that a mock or spy was called, not with what
criteria.nothing: nothing, a tautology, or only no throw

asserts_b.instructions: Of all assertions, what does the one closest to the behaviour check?

criteria.nothing: nothing, a tautology, or only no throw
criteria.interaction-only: only that a mock or spy was called, not with what
criteria.shape-only: only type, length, keys, presence, a bound, or that it is truthy or defined
criteria.input-only: only the test's own input or setup, or an output field copied straight from the input
criteria.from-code: the output, against a value from the code under test or a re-implementation of it in the test
criteria.behaviour: the output, against a value the test fixes or computes without the code

positive_a.instructions: Does an assertion need a value a do-nothing stub could not return?

criteria.true: yes: a non-zero number, a non-empty string or object, true, or an error with its message
criteria.false: no: only empty, zero, false, null, undefined, or no throw

positive_b.instructions: Does this test fail against a stub that returns nothing and never throws?

criteria.true: yes: an assertion needs a real value
criteria.false: no: it passes an empty or null result

runs_a.instructions: Does this test run, with no marker narrowing the run?

criteria.true: yes: no skip, todo, or x marker on it or its describe, and no focus-in-file flag
criteria.false: no: a skip, todo, skipIf, or x marker stops it, or an only or focus marker narrows the file

runs_b.instructions: Is this test free of skip, todo, only, and focus markers, in its head, its scope, and its flags?

criteria.true: yes: no branch, loop, early return, or catch can skip or swallow one
criteria.false: no: a branch, a loop over a value that may be empty, an early return, or a catch can skip or swallow one

isolated.instructions: Does this test pass alone and in any order, reading nothing another test sets or changes?

criteria.true: yes: what it reads is built by it, a hook, or a fixture no test changes
criteria.false: no: it reads a value another test sets or changes

deterministic.instructions: Does this test give the same result on every run and machine?

criteria.true: yes: no real clock, randomness, sleep, network, file, database, or env it does not create or fake
criteria.false: no: it reads one as it finds it

automated.instructions: Does this test pass or fail with no person involved?

criteria.true: yes: no person must set up, act, or read

restores.instructions: Does this test, or an after hook, put back every global, env variable, timer, mock, file, or shared object it changes?

criteria.true: yes: it changes none, or puts them back

resilient.instructions: Does this test reach and read the code only through its public interface?

criteria.true: yes: a public import, and it asserts a return, a throw, or an effect a caller sees
criteria.false: no: an internal import, a spy on a helper, a private or _ member, or a pinned internal call order
